findings.reason: The protected implementation is numerically correct but computes the first transformed window from nums[:k]. That slice allocates a new list containing k values during every feasibility check, so auxiliary space is O(k), not the Optimal branch's required O(1). At legal k = 10,000, measured peak traced allocation was 80,728 bytes.

The inert candidate sums the first k transformed values by indexing nums directly into the existing rolling total. It preserves the recognizable parametric-search algorithm, uses no copied window or prefix array, and reduces measured peak traced allocation at k = 10,000 to 412 bytes, about 196 times smaller. Its control flow and naming remain concise, conventional, and interview-ready.

Subtracting a candidate average turns the existence of a qualifying original subarray into the existence of a nonnegative transformed sum. The first k-value total covers start zero. For every later right endpoint, eligible_prefix advances the latest permitted start prefix and minimum_prefix retains the smallest of all eligible starts, so current_prefix - minimum_prefix tests every subarray of length at least k. Feasibility is monotone, and sixty bisections preserve the feasible lower boundary to far better than the strict source tolerance.
